cohort: The study included 48,124 patients with a single prior cesarean section, of whom 31,668 attempted a VBAC, with cases defined as complete uterine rupture during VBAC attempt and controls as VBAC attempt without uterine rupture.
finding: The complete uterine rupture frequency was low (0.63%) and was inversely associated with prior vaginal delivery, but positively associated with induction of labor and specific dystocia factors during spontaneous labor.
mod_finding: Uterine rupture was reduced with previous vaginal birth and increased with induction of labor, regardless of method, and was also associated with a low Bishop score, arrest of cervical dilatation, and oxytocin augmentation during spontaneous labor.
